title: Arkret Service Operation DTOs
description: Canonical request and response DTOs for service operations. OpenAPI components reference this artifact so SDK and conformance tooling use one schema source.

grant_jwt.description: The near-expiry DPoP-bound session grant to rotate. Presented with a DPoP holder proof for the key bound into the grant's cnf.jkt.

audience.description: Optional; MUST equal the grant's bound audience if present (audience MUST NOT change across rotation, else audience_mismatch).

device_id.description: Concrete authorized device restoring the soft-logged-out grant chain. MUST match the persisted grant device binding.

proof_kind.description: Fresh proof kind for soft-logout recovery. Current Account Authority implementations MUST accept did_bound_signature or paired_device_proof and fail closed on unsupported kinds.

request_canonical_digest.description: Digest of the soft-logout restore request transcript bound by the proof.

audience.description: MUST equal the session grant audience.

expires_at.description: MUST be after issued_at and no more than 300 seconds later.

signature.description: Detached JWS over the soft-logout proof transcript.

verification_method.description: Optional DID URL expected to match the detached JWS kid; the DID component MUST match the session grant subject.

grant_jwt.description: Rotated grant: same subject/scope/audience, cnf.jkt unchanged, fresh minutes-to-hours expiry.

session_public_key.description: JWK the rotated grant is bound to (the device holder key).

dpop_jkt.description: RFC 7638 thumbprint of the holder key (equals the grant's cnf.jkt).

previous_grant_id.description: The prior grant, single-use revoked on success.

AuthSessionLogoutRequestBody.description: Service-to-service Account Authority to Auth Server request that logs out the Auth-side session owning a ak.session.grant rotation chain.

grant_jwt.description: Session grant used to locate the Auth-side session and its rotation chain.

logout_request_digest.description: Optional digest of the validated client-visible account /logout request that caused this S2S sub-operation.

validated_at.description: When the Account Authority validated the client-visible account /logout request.

reason_code.description: Reason for logging out the Auth-side session. v1 defines only account_logout for this S2S sub-operation.

grant_chain_terminated.description: Whether the grant rotation chain is now unable to refresh, including the already-terminated idempotent case.

auth_session_logged_out.description: Whether the underlying Auth-side browser/auth session is now logged out, including the already-logged-out idempotent case.

SessionGrantIntrospectRequestBody.description: Server-to-server session-grant introspection request. Exactly one of id / grant_jwt identifies the grant.

id.description: Grant id. Mutually exclusive with grant_jwt.

grant_jwt.description: The signed grant JWT to introspect. Mutually exclusive with id.

audience.description: Audience the caller is validating the grant for; a mismatch yields status audience_mismatch.

proof.description: Optional S2S holder confirmation signed by the session key bound into the grant. Principal Servers validating /_arkret/self/* grant+DPoP requests do not require a client-carried introspection proof; they verify the request DPoP locally against the returned cnf_jkt.

proof_jwt.description: JWS over ak.session_grant.introspection_proof.v1 claims (grant_id, grant_jwt_hash, audience, challenge, issued_at, expires_at).

active.description: Whether the grant is currently valid for the requested audience. READ-ONLY: introspection never consumes the grant.

proof_required.description: Whether an additional S2S holder proof is required to confirm the grant active for this introspection request. Default Principal Server grant+DPoP validation uses the request DPoP instead of this field.

one_time_use_consumed.description: Always false: introspection is read-only and never consumes single-use state (rotation is the refresh endpoint's job).

SessionGrantIntrospectGrant.description: Non-secret grant metadata returned to the validating Principal Server. Never includes the grant JWT, refresh token, or session private key.

session_public_key.description: Session signing key (JWK) for RFC 9421 PoP verification on /_arkret/self/* (api-conventions §3.2). Server-to-server only.

cnf_jkt.description: RFC 7638 JWK SHA-256 thumbprint of the holder (DPoP) key the grant is bound to (cnf.jkt); the Principal Server uses it to verify the per-request DPoP proof on /_arkret/self/* (api-conventions §3.3). Server-to-server only.

revoked.description: Whether a live device session was revoked.

redirect_url.description: Deployment-controlled browser handoff URL. This outcome MUST NOT contain SessionGrantOutcome, ak.session.grant, or Principal local session material; client-visible grant issuance is only via SessionGrantRequestBody.proof.proof_kind=oidc_code_exchange.

AuthzCheckRequestBody.description: ak.self.authz.query.check input — local capability projection / preflight / diagnostic query. `resource` is optional because some actions (e.g. `ak.realm.create`, identity-scoped actions) have no Realm-bound target. The result is not a signed Policy Server decision and MUST NOT be used as Event auth_context, reducer accept proof, or cross-service authorization fact; dynamic policy obligations use ak.self.policy.query.check.

actor_id.description: Subject DID whose authorization is being checked.

resource.description: Optional resource selector (Realm / Strand / Space / Morph / etc.).

context.description: Optional decision context — claim presentations, frontier reference, request metadata.

AuthzCheckOutcome.description: ak.self.authz.query.check diagnostic/preflight decision. See zh/authz/capabilities.md §18. This shape may include freshness and obligation hints, but any obligation that affects reducer admission or external state MUST be re-issued and signed through PolicyCheckOutcome.

decision.description: `allow` / `hard_deny` are terminal decisions. `soft_deny` is an evaluated policy soft refusal. `quarantine` / `require_review` are Policy Server-mediated soft outcomes (the request enters async review). Transient dependency or freshness failures are reported through `freshness_state`, `reason_code`, and `retry_after_ms`, not as policy decision values.

freshness_state.description: Frontier freshness classification for revocation-sensitive decisions; see zh/authz/capabilities.md §18.2.

last_known_frontier_age_ms.description: Age of the newest revocation/auth frontier evidence used for this decision. Present when freshness_state is stale or unknown.

notary_status.description: Coarse status of the notary/frontier source used to diagnose stale or unknown revocation freshness.

reason_code.description: Registered reason code. High-risk stale or unknown revocation freshness returns revocation_freshness_unknown.

retry_after_ms.description: Set when `freshness_state ∈ {stale,unknown}` or a retryable `reason_code` is present; client SHOULD back off this amount before retry.

obligations.description: Policy server obligations (challenge / rate_limit / drop_attachment) the caller MUST satisfy before the action proceeds.

blob_ref.description: Target blob. MUST be a content-addressed ref or visible blob metadata id.

realm_id.description: Realm binding for Realm-owned blobs. Servers MUST include the same realm_id in the presign envelope and reject mismatches with blob metadata; only deployment-public/global blobs may omit this field.

max_age_seconds.description: Client-requested TTL upper bound. Server clamps to the smaller of this value, the issuing grant's `blob_presign_max_ttl_seconds` constraint, and the deployment-level cap.

purpose.description: Intended rendering / download mode. Servers MAY apply purpose-specific Content-Disposition or rate limits.

url.description: Fully-qualified URL clients can pass to browser primitives. Contains the `presign` query parameter, `blob_ref`, and a presign envelope bound to `realm_id` for Realm-owned blobs.

expires_at.description: Server-determined expiry; SHOULD be earlier than `now() + max_age_seconds`.

type.description: Backend binding type identifier (livekit / arkret-native / etc.).

backend_token.description: Opaque to Arkret protocol; type-specific (e.g. LiveKit JWT).

participant_identity.description: SFU-local short handle, scope `(call_id, focus_id, sfu_did)`. UUIDv7-form rtc_participant typed ID.

messages.description: DeviceMessageEnvelope items; not Event Envelope objects. This endpoint does not serve the durable Event timeline.

ack_token.description: Server-issued opaque acknowledgement token, REQUIRED whenever messages[] is non-empty. Covers this page plus all previously delivered messages for the authenticated device. Queue deletion happens only through ak.self.device_messages.command.ack with this token, never through the after= read cursor (client-sync.md §10.1).

next_cursor.description: Read-only continuation position; advancing it MUST NOT delete queued messages.

lost.description: SHOULD be true when unacknowledged messages were dropped (expiry or capacity) since the device's last acknowledged position; clients SHOULD trigger key recovery paths.

ack_token.description: Acknowledgement token previously issued to the same (principal_id, device_id) via an account subscribe to_device batch or a device_messages get page. Acknowledgement is cumulative and monotonic: the server prunes all delivered messages up to and including the token's bound queue position. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens MUST be rejected with invalid_param (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything. Naturally idempotent; no Idempotency-Key required.

ok.description: True when the acknowledgement was accepted, including the legal no-op case of re-acking the same or an older token (the acknowledged position MUST NOT move backward).

pruned_count.description: Number of queued messages actually deleted by this acknowledgement.

did_method.description: DID method discriminator without the did: prefix (e.g. web, webvh, key). It MUST exactly equal the method component of did; verifiers dispatch method-specific validation only after that equality check.

seq.description: Optional method sequence number when the DID method exposes one.

prev_event_digest.description: Optional previous operation hash / key-log head, when required by the DID method.

operation.description: Complete DID method-native operation, including every controller/update/recovery proof required by that method. This is not a generic JSON Patch. The selected adapter MUST validate the immutable native operation and its full history before any state mutation; transport authentication never substitutes for method-native control proof.

seq.description: New method sequence number when available.

public_base.description: Canonical service base URL: lower-case scheme and host, no query or fragment, normalized path, and exactly one trailing slash. Production deployments MUST use https; explicit development deployments MAY use http.

updateKeys.description: Exactly one active service-controlled update key. On a rotation entry it MUST open the previous entry's sole nextKeyHashes commitment; spent keys MUST NOT be reused.

nextKeyHashes.description: Exactly one sha2-256 multihash/Base58BTC commitment to a next update key generated and durably held by the service. Missing or mismatched commitments fail closed as service_prerotation_invalid.

ServiceRegistrationReceipt.description: Provider-signed stable service-registration receipt. registration_receipt_id is ak:service_registration_receipt:<lowercase hex SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt claims))>. proof is a detached JWS over the ak.service-registration-receipt-proof-v1 binding object; provider_service_id is did:webvh so consumers can verify signing-time assertionMethod authority against Provider DID history.

control_key_digest.description: Digest of the active control/update public key at version_id; this is not the next-key commitment or private recovery material.

proof.description: payload_digest = sha256(canonical_json(receipt with proof omitted)). detached_jws signs canonical_json({context:'ak.service-registration-receipt-proof-v1', payload_digest, provider_service_id, registration_receipt_id, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}); created_at MUST equal issued_at and verification_method MUST be a signing-time assertionMethod of provider_service_id.

discovery_state.description: Signed ak.{kind}.discovery payload, including its proof.

governance_proof.description: Signature proof by the resource governance key, equivalent strength to announce.discovery_state.proof.

withdrawal_ref.description: Directory-local audit reference for the withdrawal; not a registered ak:<kind> typed ID.

DirectoryTakedownAppealRequestBody.description: Resource-side appeal packet against an operator takedown; the bound fields and governance signature are normative per discovery-directory.md §8.7.

takedown_id.description: The operator takedown_id from the takedown notice.

argument_digest.description: Digest of the appeal argument / evidence bundle (sha256:<hex>).

governance_proof.description: Signature by the resource governance key or an authorized advocate, equivalent strength to withdraw.governance_proof.

DirectoryTakedownAppealOutcome.description: Signed decision receipt acknowledging an appeal submission per discovery-directory.md §8.7 step 3.

appeal_id.description: Directory-local audit reference for the appeal; not a registered ak:<kind> typed ID.

decision_receipt.description: Signed Directory decision receipt; status pending until adjudicated.

EphemeralSubmitOutcome.description:
Result of ak.ephemeral.send. `accepted=true` means the Sync Service
admitted the short-lived signal into its ephemeral fanout path. No
Event ID, actor_seq, Seal coverage, or durable receipt is minted.

dispatched_to.description: Optional implementation hint for fanout recipients queued locally.

EventView.description: Result of ak.self.events.resource.get — a single complete Event Envelope, RedactedEventView, or ReferenceLockedEventStub with optional visibility / receipt hints. Redacted / locked variants are projection-only evidence and MUST NOT be used as reducer input.

visibility.description: Caller-visible policy hint for this event (history visibility class, E2EE envelope class).

receipts.description: Event batch receipts witnessing this event, if visible.

realms.description: Filter by Realm IDs. UNION within, intersection with `actors[]`.

actors.description: Filter by Actor DIDs. UNION within, intersection with `realms[]`.

before.description: Return events strictly older than this cursor position (exclusive).

after.description: Return events strictly newer than this cursor position (exclusive).

order.description: Same semantics as the GET form `order` query parameter.

include_completeness.description: Request range-completeness attestation references covering the returned page (service-http-binding.md §3.3.6). Only effective when the service advertises events_query_range_completeness in supported_features; services that do not advertise it MUST ignore this parameter.

EventsQueryOutcome.description:
Result of ak.self.events.query.scan (GET form) and ak.self.events.query.scan_body (POST/body
form). Ordering follows the "近邻先返回" rule unless `order` was
explicitly set on the request; see service-http-binding.md §3.3.3.

prev_cursor.description: Absolute-direction cursor toward older events; pass to next request's `before=`.

next_cursor.description: Absolute-direction cursor toward newer events; pass to next request's `after=`.

has_more.description: True if more events remain in the `prev_cursor` (older) direction; SHOULD ignore `next_cursor` direction (subscribe / poll instead).

range_completeness.description: Optional. Present only when the request set include_completeness=true, the service advertises events_query_range_completeness, and at least one ak.attestation.range_completeness attestation covers the returned page's range (service-http-binding.md §3.3.6). Absence means the range is un-attested — neither an error nor a completeness confirmation. Clients verify per operations-sync.md §6.4.4 (root recompute, actor_seq_ranges check, witness_disagreement fail-closed).

attestation_refs.description: Event ids of ak.attestation.range_completeness events whose union of scopes covers the returned page. Over-coverage is legal; clients intersect scopes during verification.

attestations.description: Optional inline complete ak.attestation.range_completeness EventEnvelope objects for the referenced attestations. Every inline event's event_id MUST appear in attestation_refs and clients MUST verify the EventEnvelope signature / event_digest before using its payload. Servers MAY omit this field and let clients backfill the attestation events by id.

EventsResolveRequestBody.description: ak.self.events.query.resolve request body. At least one of event_ids or event_digests MUST be non-empty.

EventsResolveOutcome.description: ak.self.events.query.resolve result. `events[]` and `missing[]` plus optional `unauthorized[]` form a partition of the requested set.

missing.description: IDs / hashes that were requested but do not exist or are not visible (indistinguishable per visibility rules).

unauthorized.description: Optional split of missing into a separately-named bucket when policy explicitly distinguishes auth failure from non-existence.

EventsSubmitOutcome.description:
Result of ak.events.submit. Tracks per-event acceptance / duplication /
rejection along with the post-write frontier and an optional barrier
cursor for read-your-writes.

accepted.description: Event IDs that entered the accepted set for the first time. Idempotent re-submissions of identical bodies are sealed via duplicate[], not re-listed here.

duplicate.description: Event IDs whose canonical bytes matched a prior accepted event (idempotent no-op).

quarantine.description: Event IDs deferred to async / human verification.

realm_actor_frontiers.description: Post-submit authoring frontiers for accepted or duplicate Events, sorted and unique by (realm_id, actor_id).

realm_frontiers.description: Visible post-submit Realm Seal frontiers sorted and unique by realm_id.

cursor.description: Optional barrier cursor (purpose=barrier) bound to the most recently accepted event.

original_outcome.description: Present only when status="historical_only" (idempotency-cache replay after origin key revoke / binding or peer-policy change, see sync/federation.md section 8.5.1): carries the originally cached outcome verbatim as historical diagnostics. The nested outcome's status MUST NOT be "historical_only"; the top-level accepted[] MUST be empty in that case. Absent for all other status values.

EventSealSubmitOutcome.description: Result of ak.self.events.command.submit_seal after full Seal and active-device verification.

IdentityDocumentView.description: Result of ak.root.identity.document.resource.get — current DID Document plus normalized view hints.

did_document.description: Raw DID Core document with W3C field names preserved.

normalized_view.description:
Optional Arkret normalized principal view (snake_case) — derived
projection only, NOT a re-publishable DID Document. See
zh/identity/identity-did.md §6.

method_evidence.description: Method-specific proof material (e.g. did:webvh history head, witness signatures).

IdentityLogListOutcome.description: Result of ak.root.identity.log.query.list — paginated DID key-log entries for the requested DID.

next_cursor.description: Opaque continuation cursor for the next page when has_more=true.

IdentityReceiptListOutcome.description: Result of ak.root.identity.receipts.query.list — witness receipts for a DID key-log head.

threshold_met.description: True when the returned receipt set satisfies the method or deployment witness threshold for the requested head. Omitted when the registry cannot evaluate threshold policy for this query.

PolicyCheckRequestBody.description: ak.self.policy.query.check input bound to a Realm authorization context.

source_ip_digest.description: Keyed, unlinkable derivation of the request source IP (e.g. HMAC-SHA256 under a service-private, salt-epoch-rotated secret bound to the calling service_id), encoded as sha256:<64 hex>. The sha256: prefix denotes the 32-byte digest container, NOT a bare SHA-256 of the IP address; unkeyed IP hashes are forbidden. Derivation, rotation and namespace rules: zh/authz/policy-server.md §3.1. High-privacy (relay/OHTTP) deployments MAY omit this field.

PolicyCheckOutcome.description: Result of ak.self.policy.query.check — signed decision bound to authorization, policy, and membership frontier hashes.

bound_to.description: Request context covered by the policy decision signature. Allows receivers to verify a forwarded decision without guessing transcript fields.

auth_state_digest.description: Accepted authorization state hash used when producing the decision.

policy_frontier_digest.description: Policy source frontier / digest used when producing the decision.

membership_frontier_digest.description: Membership / role frontier digest used when producing the decision.

kid.description: DID URL of the Policy Server verification method.

sig.description: Detached signature over the policy decision transcript.

principal_id.description: Existing principal DID the grant is requested for. REQUIRED for every proof_kind, including oidc_code_exchange and pre_registration_handoff. Account Authorities MUST NOT derive or mint a principal DID from an OIDC subject. A first-time OIDC flow may create only a DPoP-bound account_handoff_grant until the client has completed cold-root custody, submitted a client-signed inception through account register, and established the verified principal_id binding.

agent_key_authorization_ref.description:
`ak.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay. Event ref of the accepted
`ak.agent.key.authorize` that authorized the runtime key. REQUIRED when
`proof.proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`; MUST be omitted for human session grants.

agent_scope_request.description:
`ak.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay. Narrowing hints for the
issued session scope. Service-surface requested_scope values are intersected
with the immutable provision requested_scope, accepted agent_key_scope and
endpoint/resource policy; content actions are additionally intersected with
independent effective Realm capability grants, participation, membership,
history visibility and E2EE policy. Provision mandatory constraints remain in
force at every layer. REQUIRED when `proof.proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`; MUST
be omitted for human session grants. `track_names` is a request-side narrowing
field only — the materialized session grant MUST express track scope via the
canonical `allowed_tracks` constraint, not via a new `track_names` grant.

requested_scope_disclosure.description: Optional only for the agent_key_proof branch. A runtime includes this controller-signed private disclosure when the Account Authority does not yet hold verifier-private ceiling evidence established by pairing or an authenticated private evidence transfer. If absent, the authority MUST resolve an already verified disclosure keyed by the same agent_id, DID commitment digest, verifier and audience; a service-local Agent row alone is insufficient.

dpop_binding_proof.description: `ak.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay. DPoP proof JWT for the holder key that the issued session grant will bind to. REQUIRED when `proof.proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`; the Account Authority verifies the proof and materializes the resulting JWK thumbprint into the issued grant's `cnf.jkt` / session_public_key binding.

applet_delegation.description: Applet-specific delegated session binding. When present, the session grant, proof digest, persistence row, introspection metadata, and revoke selector are bound to the same applet_id, effective_scope, and registration_epoch.

proof_kind.description:
`agent_key_proof` selects the `ak.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay branch.
Implementations MUST route `agent_key_proof` to an independent validator and MUST NOT
fall back to password / OIDC / passkey validators for this branch.

issuer.description: OIDC issuer selected from ServiceDescribe.auth_metadata.methods[].issuer. Required when proof_kind is oidc_code_exchange.

client_id.description: OIDC public client id selected from the advertised auth method. Required when proof_kind is oidc_code_exchange.

redirect_uri.description: Redirect URI used in the authorization request. Required when proof_kind is oidc_code_exchange.

state.description: OIDC authorization response state. Required when proof_kind is oidc_code_exchange.

nonce.description: OIDC nonce bound to the authorization request and id_token. Required when proof_kind is oidc_code_exchange.

authorization_code.description: OIDC authorization code. Account Authority exchanges this code at the issuer token_endpoint when proof_kind is oidc_code_exchange.

code_verifier.description: PKCE code_verifier corresponding to the authorization request. Required when proof_kind is oidc_code_exchange.

verification_method.description:
`ak.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay. DID URL of the runtime
signing key (`<agent_id>#<key-fragment>`). REQUIRED when
`proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`; the DID component MUST bit-identically equal
`principal_id` after stripping the fragment / query — otherwise the endpoint
returns `verification_method_principal_mismatch`. MUST be omitted for human
proof kinds.

signature.description: Proof-kind authority signature over the canonical request transcript. For pre_registration_handoff it MUST be produced by the same holder key as the Authorization credential's cnf.jkt and the request DPoP proof.

allOf.description:
Machine-enforceable agent_key_proof branch selector. When `proof.proof_kind` is
`agent_key_proof`, the request MUST carry the `ak.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay
fields (`agent_key_authorization_ref`, `agent_scope_request`, `dpop_binding_proof`,
`proof.verification_method`) and MAY carry a private requested_scope_disclosure
when the verifier has no accepted cache; when it is any other enum value, agent-only fields
MUST be absent. SDKs and server-side validators MUST reject violations at
schema-validation time, not at proof-validator time.

Machine-enforceable OIDC code exchange branch. Account Authority, not the client, exchanges the authorization code at the issuer token_endpoint and validates issuer, state, nonce, redirect_uri, the REQUIRED existing principal_id binding, device binding and request canonical digest before issuing SessionGrantOutcome. OIDC identity alone never creates a principal DID. proof_kind=pre_registration_handoff instead authenticates with Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header; the body MUST omit all OIDC exchange fields, and grant issuance still requires the requested principal_id to be the handoff account's verified binding.

proof_jwt.description: RFC 9449 DPoP proof JWT over the session-grant issuance endpoint. For agent_key_proof issuance this proves possession of the holder key before the Account Authority returns the session grant.

session_grant.description: Short-lived bearer/session grant bound to the requested principal, device and audience.

grant_id.description: Stable id of the issued session grant. Returned for every grant (human and agent) so the client can reference, refresh, introspect or revoke this exact grant without re-parsing the opaque session_grant. Mirrors SessionGrantRefreshOutcome.grant_id.

session_public_key.description: JWK of the holder/session key the grant is bound to (the device holder key). The client needs this to perform RFC 9421 PoP and to derive the DPoP cnf.jkt for /_arkret/self/* requests (api-conventions.md §3.2 / §3.3); returning it at issue time avoids a mandatory introspect round-trip before the first self-path request. Equals the grant's bound session_public_key for both human and agent grants. Mirrors SessionGrantRefreshOutcome.session_public_key.

audience.description: Audience the grant is bound to (the Principal Server / service the grant is valid for). MUST equal the grant's bound audience. Mirrors SessionGrantRefreshOutcome.audience.

scope_details.description:
`ak.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay. Materialized narrow scope
actually granted to the agent runtime session. Service-surface scope is the
intersection of immutable provision requested_scope, accepted agent_key_scope,
session requested_scope and endpoint/resource policy; content actions are
additionally constrained by independent effective Realm capability grants,
participation, membership, history visibility and E2EE policy. Provision
mandatory constraints remain in force. Present iff the request was the
`proof.proof_kind="agent_key_proof"` branch; absent for human session grants.

participation.description: `ak.profile.agent_participation_policy.v1` overlay (service-surface.md §10.1). Present when the agent session scope covers participation-aware scope. Each entry is isomorphic to agent_participation_entry ({participation_scope, selection, ceiling, effective}). The runtime MUST treat this array as a behavioral contract; the server still enforces capability grants, dispatcher gates and reducer checks as the hard boundary.

ActorDid.description: Bare DID used as a Arkret actor/principal identifier. DID URL fragments belong in verification_method, not actor_id/principal_id.

message_id.description: Sender-assigned stable identity copied unchanged into DeviceMessageEnvelope.message_id. Reusing the same sender-scoped message_id with different canonical target content MUST fail with duplicate_conflict (reason message_id_conflict).

allOf.description:
Actor-supplied ak.self.events.command.submit input envelope. It reuses the base Event
shape for actor intent fields but forbids reducer-managed accepted-output
projections such as actor_kind and effective_scope. Services stamp those
fields only after accept and expose them on read/query/sync envelopes.

RealmActorFrontierView.description: Deterministic authoring frontier for exactly one (realm_id, actor_id) chain. frontier_event_ids is the complete sorted sibling set at next_actor_seq - 1.

frontier_event_ids.description: Bytewise UTF-8 sorted, duplicate-free complete accepted sibling set at the highest actor sequence.

RealmSealFrontierView.description: Current accepted Realm Seal head used only for seal_basis and seal_ref authoring.

ActorAggregateFrontierView.description: Read-only actor history aggregate. It has no single sequence or head and cannot be used for Event authoring.

realms.description: Visible Realm frontiers sorted by realm_id with no duplicate realm_id.

EventsActorCasConflictDetails.description: Closed details for an authenticated, visible actor-chain cas_conflict that proves the submitted Event was not accepted and its signed basis is stale.

EventsFrontierAccountClientState.description: Account-client ak.self.events.query.frontier response. For a managed Agent PCR whose accepted Events are ahead of its accepted Seal, frontier remains the last accepted controller-device-signed Seal and receipts includes `{kind: ak.managed_agent_pcr.seal_head.v1, seal: Seal}` so the controller can author the successor; the service must never synthesize that device Seal.

ManagedAgentPcrSealHeadReceipt.description: Accepted controller-device-signed managed Agent PCR Seal head returned when accepted Events are ahead of Seal coverage. The service relays this exact Seal and MUST NOT synthesize or sign it.

EventsFrontierFederationPeerState.description: Federation peer ak.peer.events.query.frontier response. Requires S2S signed trust-domain headers.

heads.description: Current federation-visible head Event IDs for this Realm.

max_hlc.description: Maximum HLC observed by the issuer at this frontier, when available.

frontier_root.description: Hash commitment returned to an authorized federation peer.

actor_seq_upper_bounds.description: Per-actor sequence upper bounds returned to an authorized federation peer.

witness_receipts.description: Optional witness or receipt-service attestations over the observed frontier.

signature.description: Service signature over the peer frontier response.

EventReadItem.description: A readable event item. Complete EventEnvelope is the only reducer input shape. RedactedEventView and ReferenceLockedEventStub are projection/completeness evidence for callers that may know the source event exists but may not receive its full canonical payload bytes.

event_digest.description: Digest of the complete canonical Event Envelope bytes with proofs and unsigned removed. The caller cannot recompute it from this redacted view; it is a commitment used with inclusion / availability proofs.

payload_digest.description: Optional digest commitment to the canonical payload object before masking.

inclusion_proof.description: Optional proof that the committed event_digest is included in an Event set / Seal / range-completeness root visible to the caller.

reducer_input.description: Redacted views are projection-only evidence and MUST NOT be fed into a reducer as Event Envelope input.

event_id.description: Present only when the source event id is already visible to the caller; omitted when even the event id would distinguish target existence.

realm_id.description: The source Realm boundary visible to the caller. Target Realm identifiers hidden by reference-disclosure policy MUST NOT appear.

event_digest.description: Optional source-event commitment when the source event is known but its payload is locked.

reason_code.description: Reasons that would reveal target existence MUST be collapsed to not_found_or_unauthorized for unauthorized callers.

inclusion_proof.description: Optional non-disclosing proof commitment. MUST NOT contain hidden target refs or target Realm metadata.

reducer_input.description: Locked stubs are projection-only evidence and MUST NOT be fed into a reducer as Event Envelope input.

EventsSubmitBatchRequestBody.description: Batch ak.self.events.command.submit request used by account clients.

signer_key_evidence.description: Source-Principal-Server attestation of active participant device keys needed to verify original Event proofs. This transport-only evidence is covered by the outer HTTP Message Signature and never changes the Event envelope.

FederationServiceBindingRef.description:
Request-level service binding snapshot carried by federation
service-to-service ak.peer.events.command.submit calls. This is metadata for the
receiver to verify the sender's delivery decision; client writes omit it.

reducer_profile_digest.description: SHA-256 over the Arkret canonical JSON bytes of the locally rebuilt content-addressed resolved_digest_input closure declared by artifacts/registry/reducer-profile-registry.json. Receivers MUST independently resolve local event-kind, schema, fixture, and reducer-contract content and reject the whole federation batch with reducer_profile_mismatch on mismatch.

ProjectionAssignedToRelation.description: Read-model edge backing a Strand assigned_to Relation. relation_id is needed by clients to tombstone the assignment; actor_id mirrors the Relation to_ref.

title.description: Derived display title from plaintext-visible Strand metadata.title; null when metadata is encrypted or hidden from the service profile.

summary.description: Derived display summary from plaintext-visible Strand metadata.summary; null when metadata is encrypted or hidden from the service profile.

board_space_id.description: Derived board Space id from ak.component.strand.position.v1; not canonical Strand object state.

list_space_id.description: Derived list Space id from ak.component.strand.position.v1; not canonical Strand object state.

rank.description: Derived rank within list_space_id from ak.component.strand.position.v1.

assigned_actor_ids.description: Derived current assignee Actor DIDs from visible active Relation(relation_kind=assigned_to, from_ref=strand_id). Empty or absent means the Strand is unassigned for this projection caller. This is read-model state, not canonical Strand object metadata.

assigned_to_relations.description: Read-only active assigned_to Relation edges backing assigned_actor_ids. Clients use relation_id to tombstone assignments.

is_default.description: DERIVED, not independent storage: true iff strand_id == the parent Realm projection's default_strand_id (the authoritative pointer written by ak.realm.set_default_strand). The projector computes this from Realm.default_strand_id; a stale/dangling pointer never resolves to is_default=true because the reducer rejects set_default_strand against a non-existent Strand. Clients identify the Realm's default discussion Strand deterministically from this flag (or equivalently from Realm.default_strand_id) and MUST NOT infer the default from any Strand-reuses-Realm-UUID or other implementation detail. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md (default-Strand discovery).

kind.description: Space kind such as `board`, `list`, `folder`, or a profile-registered kind.

ServiceId.description: Bare DID identifying a service endpoint.

SnapshotBootstrap.description: Optional ak.self.events.query.scan acceleration hint for federation pull / backfill. snapshot_ref is an external pointer and MUST equal the Snapshot manifest id. Verifier MUST validate signature, state_digest, snapshot_frontier, chunk digests, created_by, created_at, and authority_binding before use (manifest fields are bound by the manifest signature transcript — see schemas/snapshot.schema.json).

snapshot_ref.description: External pointer to the Snapshot manifest; MUST equal schemas/snapshot.schema.json#/properties/id.

created_by.description: DID of the snapshot issuer; bound by the manifest signature transcript.

created_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp ending in 'Z' when the manifest was sealed; bound by the manifest signature transcript.

authority_binding.description: Snapshot issuer authority evidence bound by the manifest signature transcript; mirrors schemas/snapshot.schema.json#/properties/authority_binding.
